title: feat: Cloudron package for Orbit 0.2.1 (testing)
body:
## What

A Cloudron package for [Orbit](https://github.com/coollabsio/orbit) 0.2.1 (commit `fe9dce7`, Apache-2.0): self-hosted tasks, docs and team chat with an MCP server. It is released as a **testing** package for small teams.

- **Runtime:** upstream's release binary, copied from `ghcr.io/coollabsio/orbit:0.2.1` pinned by digest, onto `cloudron/base:6.0.1`. supervisord runs Orbit on `127.0.0.1:8080` and nginx on 8000. nginx marks requests as HTTPS for Orbit's production mode and trusts `X-Forwarded-For` only from Cloudron's proxy (the default gateway). Orbit trusts only nginx. No wildcard proxy ranges are trusted.
- **Data:** SQLite in WAL mode, declared as a `localstorage` SQLite path so backups are consistent. Attachments, Orbit's own snapshots and a generated app key are under `/app/data`. `/app/data/orbit.env` accepts only upload, job-concurrency and rate-limit settings.
- **Mail:** there is no env config upstream (coollabsio/orbit#66). `orbit-mail-settings` prints the Cloudron relay values to enter in Admin → Email.
- **Operator commands:** `orbit`, `orbit-offline` (stops the server for database-exclusive commands such as `recovery-link`) and `orbit-setup-link`.
- **Listing:** `DESCRIPTION.md`, `POSTINSTALL.md`, `CHANGELOG`, Orbit's logo as the icon, an original hero, and four store slides from real screenshots. `iconUrl` and `mediaLinks` are pinned to `435f410`; all six URLs return 200 `image/png`.
- **Docs:** `README.md`, `DESIGN.md` (how the artwork was made, plus the privacy and claims review), `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md` (decisions, upstream limits, local and Cloudron results) and `docs/PUBLISHING.md` (pipeline and test-install checklist).
- **Workflows:** a catalog-publication caller pinned to aidevops `6dfe5be` (v3.39.131), with `aidevops_ref` equal to the pin. It runs `test/package-test.sh` and ShellCheck. There is also a tag-release caller.

## Known limits

- No OpenID Connect, so no Cloudron SSO (coollabsio/orbit#65).
- The Mail section is "Coming soon" with mock data. It is not a webmail client.
- The package is x86-64 only for now.
- An upload over the limit (25 MiB by default) returns 502 from the package's nginx rather than Orbit's 413, because Orbit closes the connection before reading the body. Nothing is stored, and chat shows "Upload failed." either way. Request buffering did not fix it, so it is documented in `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`: passed. `shellcheck` on all scripts: clean.
- Local amd64 image, run under emulation behind TLS. Health was ready and the first-run setup worked. Tasks, docs and chat worked. Upgrading a 0.2.0 data directory to 0.2.1 kept the data. The app key was created once and reused. Shutdown was clean. Test email went through an authenticated relay and still worked after a restart and after the upgrade. A SQLite dump and restore passed the integrity and FTS5 checks.
- Cloudron test install (Cloudron 10.1.6, CLI 9.0.4, built on the server from `77821a1`), with a root user and an invited member:
  - TLS and `/health/ready`, `orbit-setup-link`, root account and workspace.
  - Client addresses are the browser's, through Cloudron's proxy.
  - Chat messages and doc co-editing appear live for the other user, also after 330 seconds idle.
  - A 20 MiB upload attaches; a 30 MiB upload is refused (see Known limits).
  - Mail through the Cloudron relay: test email, invitation (accepted), password reset.
  - MCP over OAuth with a scripted public client: discovery, dynamic registration, consent, PKCE, `initialize`, `tools/list`, `list_projects`, and 401 after revocation.
  - Restart, Cloudron backup → clone (data present, stored SMTP secret decrypts, clone mail works with its own values) and `cloudron update` all kept the data and settings.
  - Idle memory: about 30 MiB per container and 54 MiB resident for Orbit, against 1 GiB.
- **Not done:** arm64, load from several people, an update across Orbit versions on Cloudron (checked locally), and an MCP client app such as Claude Code. Details are in `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`.

## Publication

Nothing is published by this PR or by merging it. The catalog workflow publishes only when the repository variable `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED` is `true`, and that variable is unset. Squash merging is fine: the pinned listing commit stays reachable through this PR's ref, as in the LibreCrawl package.

title: docs: record published 0.1.0 check and fix attestation command
body:
## What

Docs only, after the first catalog publication of 0.1.0 (run 42319765362, release v0.1.0):

- `README.md`: the Status row still said "not yet qualified on a Cloudron server". It now links the Cloudron 10.1.6 results, and a new Install row gives the `cloudron install --versions-url` command.
- `docs/PUBLISHING.md`: the provenance commands failed as written. The attestations are signed by the reusable aidevops workflow, so `gh attestation verify` needs `--signer-workflow`. With `--repo` alone it exits with `verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"`. The category-220 link text now reads "Community Packages", the forum's current name for it.
- `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`: records the check of the published image (install from the catalog URL, anonymous pull, provenance, health), done after the merge.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`: "Package static checks passed".
- Published-image check on Cloudron 10.1.6: `cloudron install --versions-url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-orbit-app/main/CloudronVersions.json` installed 0.1.0 from `ghcr.io/marcusquinn/cloudron-orbit-app@sha256:2e3de9a6b4fa4bb16d59b282147c13d67e60bad9f920d5f5d9b26a9c006cb7a0`. `/health/ready` returned 200 (`application/json`) and `/` returned 200. The app was uninstalled afterwards.
- An anonymous GHCR token fetch for that digest returned 200 `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`.
- The documented `gh attestation verify` command, with `--source-digest 6f94e7f…` and `--signer-digest 6dfe5be…`, verified the image digest. The same command without `--signer-workflow` failed, as now described in the docs.

## Publication impact

None. The manifest, `DESCRIPTION.md` and the version are unchanged. On main, preflight finds 0.1.0 already in the catalog and takes the reconcile path. The release job then sees v0.1.0 already published and exits without changes.

title: chore: resync framework workflow to aidevops canonical caller
body:
## Summary

Resync `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml` to the canonical aidevops caller template
(reusable-workflow pattern, GH#20649 + GH#20727).

**Classification before**: `NO-WORKFLOW`
**Ref**: `@main`

## Why

The aidevops framework ships managed GitHub Actions workflows as reusable
workflows. Downstream repos carry ~45-line callers that delegate all logic
to the configured aidevops reusable workflow repository/ref.

This PR brings this repo in line with the canonical template, eliminating
drift and unblocking automatic updates when the framework evolves.

## How to verify

After merge, trigger an event matching the workflow triggers. Framework
scripts are fetched at runtime via a secondary checkout — no
`.agents/scripts/` files are needed in this repo.

## Rollback

If the workflow breaks, revert this PR. The previous workflow is preserved
in git history at the parent commit.

Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (see marcusquinn/aidevops#20649).

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->
